rationales.1: All three counts carry full qualified copy and a complete specs table with all three flagged figures present; the visual companion is a simple ornament rather than an explanatory diagram, but nothing is missing or degenerate.
rationales.2: The H1 ('Three counts: bag, unfold, water') names the page's structure rather than the product itself, deferring the product/audience statement to the subhead a line down.
rationales.3: All three flagged figures carry their qualifiers, and the page goes further by explicitly disclaiming that 'the dial is an ornament and is not timing your visit,' pre-empting confusion its own device risked creating.
rationales.4: Skip control is present as the prominent filled header button, and the page's short length itself further reduces any need to hunt for pacing control.
rationales.5: Clean and bold, but leans on a heavier slab-style face for numerals and price against a plainer sans headline, a higher-risk pairing that reads slightly more poster-like than product literature.
rationales.6: The slowest mobile LCP of the three (964ms, still comfortably under the 2500ms budget) and the largest desktop frame-time overage (17.1ms vs. the 16.7ms line), though the margin is trivial and the reduced-motion fallback is equally graceful.
rationales.7: The elapsed-time ring is an honest device but visualizes a time metric rather than the physical bag-to-hull-to-water transformation the brief's anti-spectacle test asks the motion to demonstrate; static evidence doesn't fully settle how this reads once running.
rationales.8: Both declared breaks (elapsed-time ornament in place of a hero image; jump-link specs instead of scrolling) are cleanly executed with no undeclared breaks visible, and purchase mechanics stay conventional.
rationales.9: Specific and conceptually tight copy ('the pitch and the proof are the same object'), though the counting conceit occasionally reads more like a formal device than boat-specific voice.
rationales.10: The page is explicitly built short with separate 'Specs' and 'Price' jump links so a returning visitor need not scroll a narrative at all, most directly answering the corpus concern about visit-two friction.
